entry.description: AI-assisted formal audit and corrected statements for Markman’s Weil-classes paper. The primary source reports: The maintainer reports an AI-produced formal audit of arXiv:2502.03415v2 that identifies eleven statements as false or misprinted as printed and formalizes the closest corrected versions: Proposition 1.3.1; the odd-n case of Lemma 2.2.1; the Spin/GL image claim; Remark 2.2.5; signs in Remark 2.3.1 and Lemma 6.3.2; equation (8.1.2), which needs End_Q(X)=Q; the involution and a coefficient in section 8.1; a group in Lemma 2.2.2; and Remark 10.1.2(1) for d=0. The source also reports a misprinted basis in Example 10.2.2, documents wrong proof steps and named gaps, supplies corrected or alternative arguments, and says none of these changes affects Theorems 1.4.1 or 1.5.1 or Corollary 1.6.1. The primary source directly reports this AI involvement: CREDITS.md and formalization.yaml name Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, report one main session with 56 sub-agents over two rounds, and say AI agents wrote the Lean code/documents, reviewed statements against the TeX, compared proofs with the paper, and verified the audit. The human maintainer chose scope and approved eight substantive statement corrections; three obvious slips were corrected and reported. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 003, The quasi-Riemann hypothesis. OpenAI's 6 October 2026 catalogue reports: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including \zeta(s), is zero-free in \Re s\gt 7/8, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over \mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3}). A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane \Re s\gt 11/12. OpenAI says an internal frontier model produced the released result package; its repository warns that results have different verification statuses and that some unformalized results could have issues. OpenAI links a Lean companion for the family, but this run did not replay it or establish statement correspondence. This source-attributed record remains provisional=1. Dave Goldblatt reports that Lean default-kernel and independent nanoda-kernel checks accepted OAI.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re for Mathlib riemannZeta, with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and no sorryAx or Lean.ofReduceBool. This is source-reported independent replay of the zeta formal statement only, not all Dirichlet/Hecke claims or independent analytic correspondence review. Further checking: Check the broader Dirichlet and Hecke claims and paper-to-formal analytic correspondence separately; obtain a second fresh-clone reproduction by another operator. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 014, Restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan. OpenAI's 6 October 2026 catalogue reports: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over \overline{\mathbb F}_q under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses. Over global function fields, proves Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions, and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic unramified component. Assuming the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition, constructs global Arthur enhancements of occurring cuspidal excursion parameters for split connected semisimple groups at full finite level, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia. OpenAI says an internal frontier model produced the released result package; its repository warns that results have different verification statuses and that some unformalized results could have issues. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 021, A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal’s function. OpenAI's 6 October 2026 catalogue reports: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of Ck^2 consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss. OpenAI says an internal frontier model produced the released result package; its repository warns that results have different verification statuses and that some unformalized results could have issues. OpenAI links a Lean companion for the family, but this run did not replay it or establish statement correspondence. This source-attributed record remains provisional=1. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 022, The weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 034, Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity. OpenAI's catalogue, publicly updated on 8 October 2026, reports: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample. It also proves projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting. A further result resolves the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs over such fields in each fixed dimension and for each fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components. entry.description: OpenAI Math family 036, Numerical semiampleness and generalized minimal models. OpenAI's catalogue, publicly updated on 8 October 2026, reports: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints K_X+B+M with K_X+B pseudo-effective and M nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact Kähler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott–Chern cohomology in the latter case.
